title: Conditions of Advance under the Operating Lines of Credit Loan Agreement
content:
An advance on any of the Operating Lines of Credit is booked only when every condition of advance below is met on the record; otherwise it is declined in full.

## Conditions of advance in force

1. **Line status.** An advance may be booked only while the line is in active status.
2. **Advance period.** An advance may be booked only when its effective date is on or before the advance cutoff date recorded on the line. No grace days are added beyond the cutoff date (a grace allowance of 0 calendar days). The days are counted as calendar days after the anchor date, the anchor date itself being day 0, and the last counted day still qualifies.
3. **Size.** An advance must be at least the product's smallest advance and no larger than the available credit, except as permitted under the overadvance rules of the product.
4. **Daily channel limits.** Advances requested through online banking or the mobile app may not take that channel's total for the effective date above the product's online daily limit, and advances requested by phone may not take that channel's total above the product's phone daily limit; branch advances have no daily channel limit.
5. **No partial booking.** An advance that fails any limit is declined in full, never booked in part.
6. **Effective date.** A request received on a business day after the product's same-day cutoff time, Central time, or on a weekend or Federal Reserve holiday, takes effect the next business day.
7. **Delivery of proceeds.** Proceeds go to the member's checking account, by check, by wire (charged the product's wire fee per wire) or, only where the product allows supplier-direct proceeds, directly to the named input supplier.

The status and the advance cutoff date are read from the association's record of the line the advance is drawn on, before the advance is booked.

## Conditions no longer in force

- "For a product that requires a borrowing base, an advance may be booked only when its effective date is no later than the product's certificate staleness period in calendar days after the as-of date of the line's most recent borrowing base certificate." — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis.
- "The available credit of a revolving product is the commitment (or, when the product requires a borrowing base, the lower of the commitment and the borrowing base of the most recent certificate) minus outstanding principal; the available credit of a non-revolving product is the commitment minus all advances booked in the current term, whatever has been repaid." — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis.

## Advance period boundary (hypothetical dates)

| Advance cutoff date on the line | Effective date of the advance | Within the advance period |
|---|---|---|
| 30 November | 29 November | Yes |
| 30 November | 30 November (day 0, the last qualifying day) | Yes |
| 30 November | 1 December | No — declined in full |

## Channel limit case (hypothetical)

On an ExpressLine Operating Credit, whose phone limit is USD 25,000 a day, a member who has drawn USD 20,000 by phone for today's effective date asks by phone for USD 6,000 more. The phone total would reach USD 26,000, above the limit, so the USD 6,000 advance is declined in full; it is not booked at USD 5,000.

superseded_clauses: The available credit of a revolving product is the commitment (or, when borrowing_base_required is true, the lower of the commitment and the borrowing_base_amount of the most recent certificate) minus outstanding principal; the available credit of a non-revolving product is the commitment minus all advances booked in the current term (operating_msr_term_advances), whatever has been repaid.

For a product that requires a borrowing base, an advance may be booked only when its effective date is no later than bbc_staleness_days calendar days after the as-of date of the line's most recent borrowing base certificate.
